rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROVISIONS OF THE 1992 INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION ON CIVIL LIABILITY FOR OIL POLLUTION DAMAGE AND THE 1992 INTERNATIONAL CONVENTION ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN INTERNATIONAL FUND FOR COMPENSATION FOR OIL POLLUTION DAMAGE, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Oil Pollution Compensation Act
rows.abstract: \"Oil Pollution Compensation Act\". To protect the country's marine wealth, this bill proposes to adopt and implement the provisions of the 1992 International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage and the 1992 International Convention on the Establishment of an International Fund for Compensation for Oil Pollution Damage. The two (2) conventions provide a system of compensation for pollution damage caused by a ship as a result of an incident, and for the cost of recovery measures to prevent or minimize such damage.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF DRUG REHABILITATION CENTER IN EVERY REGION OF THE COUNTRY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The illegal drug menace has penetrated almost all sectors of society. This measure seeks to establish a drug rehabilitation center in every region in the country to provide medical and psychiatric treatment to drug dependents. By making medical facilities easily accessible, drug dependents are provided an opportunity to become useful and productive members of the community again.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL LAND ADMINISTRATION AUTHORITY, RATIONALIZING THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES RELATED TO LAND ADMINISTRATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Land Administration Reform Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Land Administration Reform Act of 2004\". The land administration powers and functions in the country are currently dispersed among different government agencies. This bill seeks to reform the existing land administration and management system by consolidating and streamlining the land administration functions and powers within a single government agency to be known as the National Land Administration Reform Authority.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE CRIME OF BETRAYAL OF DUTY IN THE CUSTODY OF PRISONERS PROVIDING FOR ADDITIONAL RULES ON THE IMPRISONMENT, DETENTION, CONFINEMENT AND CUSTODY OF PRISONERS AND DETAINEES, SPECIFYING ADDITIONAL WORK AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL CHARGED WITH THE CUSTODY OF SUCH PRISONERS AND STATING THE PENALTIES THEREFORE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In many instances, a government official or employee commits the crime of infidelity in the custody of prisoner because the penalty for such  act is light and the inducement of a bribe is too tempting. A guard who frees an inmate not only participates post litem to the commission of the crime but also turns traitor to the government. This bill seeks to define the crime of betrayal of duty in the custody of prisoners and impose stiffer penalties on officials who betray their duty as caretakers of prisoners.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bills seeks to abolish the death penalty and to substitute the same with the penalty of reclusion perpetua or life imprisonment. The death penalty is the most cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment and it has no place in civilized society.

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING ENFORCED OR INVOLUNTARY DISAPPEARANCE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Anti-Enforced or Involuntary Disappearance Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Enforced or Involuntary Disappearance Act of 2004\". The State resorts to involuntary disappearance to stifle dissent and to silence political activists. While it may no longer be rampant, it remains unbated with not a single case having been resolved. This bill seeks, among others, to adopt the United Nations definition of enforced or involuntary disappearance, to consider involuntary disappearance as a continuing offense as long as the perpetrators continue to conceal the whereabouts of the persons who have disappeared and to disallow time limitation for the prosecution of persons responsible for the commission of involuntary disappearance.

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-12-04, transmitted to on 2006-12-07 and received by the Senate on 2006-12-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE OPEN HIGH SCHOOL SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Open High School System Act of 2000
rows.abstract: \"Open High School System Act of 2000\". This measure seeks to make secondary education available to out-of-school youth and adults who have graduated from the elementary but are unable to go to high school because of geographic and socio-economic constraints. It proposes to use print, radio, television and computer-based communications, satellite broadcasting, teleconferencing and other multi-media learning and teaching technologies that allow students to study on their own without having to regularly attend classes in conventional classrooms.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TAX BENEFITS TO PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS, CORPORATIONS, PARTNERSHIPS OR INSTRUMENTALITIES, DONATING TO A SCHOLARSHIP FOUNDATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: As an incentive to donors to scholarship foundations, this bill seeks to exempt any individual, corporation, partnership or instrumentality donating to a scholarship foundation from paying donor's tax. It provides that the total amount of the donations shall be deducted from the personal or corporate tax imposed on the donor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE SCHOOL HEALTH AND NUTRITION PROGRAM (SHNP) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: School Health and Nutrition Modernization Act
rows.abstract: \"School Health and Nutrition Modernization Act\". This bill seeks to modernize and upgrade the School Health and Nutrition Program by prioritizing the following concerns: a. the recruitment of school health and nutrition personnel; b. the upgrading of the salary of health and nutrition personnel to be at par with their counterparts in other Departments; c. the provision of equipment, medical and dental supplies and medicines; and d. health examination of all GRade I entrants and provision of supplementary feeding to Grade I pupils.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING POST-HARVEST FACILITIES TO RICE FARMERS
rows.title_short: Post-Harvest Facilities Support Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Post-Harvest Facilities Support Act of 2004\". The bill provides for the government, in consultation with farmer cooperatives, to construct warehouses and rice mills in every rice-producing municipality and city, and to provide the equipment and machinery necessary to operate these warehouse and rice mills. It aims to raise farm incomes to a level high enough to allow farmers to satisfy their material needs and enhance their self-esteem.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH AND POPULATION MANAGEMENT COUNCIL FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF AN INTEGRATED POLICY ON REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH RELATIVE TO SUSTAINABLE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT AND POPULATION MANAGEMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: As a preventive measure against abortion, this bill provides for timely and accurate information and education on reproductive health as well as ready access to safe, adequate and affordable reproductive health care services. It guarantees freedom of choice of individuals and couples on the number and spacing of their children. It sets the ideal family size to two (2) children.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF STUDENTS
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for Students
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Students\". The proposed Magna Carta for Students seeks to respect, protect and fulfill the rights of students in the secondary, post-secondary, graduate and post-graduate courses. Among others, it provides for student representation in the governing board and other policy-making bodies of the school, the creation of multi-sectoral School Fee Board, the right to organize and run an autonomous student council, and the right to publish and circulate an independent school paper. The Magna Carta also seeks to penalize any violation of the rights of students.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2005-03-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE CHARTER OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACADEMY (LGA), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT OF 1990, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Local Government Academy (LGA) Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Local Government Academy (LGA) Act of 2004\". The Local Government Academy (LGA) is tasked to train and improve the managerial skills and technical capability of local government officials and personnel to properly equip them with the demands of their position. This measure aims to strengthen the LGA and transform it to a more autonomous corporate body with the end in view of making its program more responsive to the needs of its clients.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D013
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO UPGRADE THE POSITION OF SECRETARIES TO THE SANGGUNIAN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 469(A), OF CHAPTER 3, BOOK III, TITLE 5, ARTICLE 1 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The functions, duties and responsibilities of the secretaries of the local sanggunians are vital to the program of local government units. This bill seeks to elevate the position of all secretaries to the sanggunians to an appropriate rank with a commensurate salary.

rows.author: D013
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE LOCAL SANGGUNIANS, EXCEPT THE SANGGUNIANG BARANGAYS THE POWER TO CONDUCT INQUIRIES, IN AID OF LEGISLATION, TO ISSUE SUBPOENA AND TO PUNISH FOR CONTEMPT ANY PERSON WHO REFUSES TO OBEY SUCH PROCESS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 447, 458 AND 468 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to expressly grant the local sangguniang panlalawigans the power to issue subpoena and subpoena duces tecum. Although the power to issue subpoena and subpoena duces tecum is impliedly granted to the local sangguniang panlalawigans by virtue of the statutory grant of delegated legislative power, there is a need to epxressly grant the same because the subpoena power is judicial in character. Allowing local legislative bodies to exercise this power without express statutory basis will impinge on the principle of separation of powers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE HEALTH CARE DELIVERY SYSTEM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Health Care Delivery Modernization Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Health Care Delivery Modernization Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to modernize the health care delivery system in the country to a level where it can fully and effectively perform its constitutional mandate to protect and promote the right to health of the citizenry and instill health consciousness among them. The proposed modernization program consists of several components that will ultimately phase out the antiquated system of health care delivery to complement state-of-the-art equipment and technology.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-30, transmitted to on 2006-09-07 and received by the Senate on 2006-09-07

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-30, transmitted to on 2006-09-07 and received by the Senate on 2006-09-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATIONS OF HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATIONS (HMOs), PROVIDING THEM INCENTIVES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Health Maintenance Organizations Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Health Maintenance Organizations Act of 2004\". The measure proposes to grant health maintenance organizations (HMOs) reasonable incentives to encourage the participation of the private sector in the government's endeavor to make health care available to all. It also seeks to establish the operating guidelines for HMOs to rectify the gross inequality of bargaining power that currently characterizes the relationship of HMOs with their members and health care providers.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO SET ASIDE THE FORTY PERCENT (40%) SHARE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS FROM THE VALUE ADDED TAX (VAT) COLLECTED BY THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS FOR THE BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE TO AUGMENT THE FUNDING EXCLUSIVELY FOR BASIC HEALTH CARE SERVICES AND FACILITIES DEVOLVED TO PROVINCES AND HIGHLY URBANIZED CITIES
rows.title_short: Setting Aside Forty Percent (40%) Share of LGU's From the Value Added Tax (VAT) For Basic Health Care Services and Facilities Devolved to Provinces and Highly Urbanized Cities
rows.abstract: This bill mandates the national government agencies concerned to set aside the forty percent (40%) share of local government units in the total value added tax collected by the Bureau of Customs for the Bureau of Internal Revenue to augment the funding requirement for basic health care services and facilities devolved to provinces and highly urbanized cities. The share of each province or highly urbanized city, with devolved health care services and facilities, shall be distributed equitably on the basis of population within its territorial jurisdiction.

rows.author: C077
rows.mother_status: Unfinished Business (Period of Sponsorship)
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING CERTAIN LOCAL OFFICIALS TO FILL THE VACANCY IN THE OFFICES OF THE GOVERNOR OR MAYOR AND VICE-GOVERNOR OR VICE-MAYOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 44 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Section 44 of the Local Government Code delineates the line of succession in case of vacancy in the offices of the governor or mayor, vice-governor, vice-mayor and the sanggunian member. It is, however, silent as to whether the official, who is next in line of succession, can fill the very same vacant position he is prohibited by law to serve beyond three consecutive terms. The bill seeks to amend the aforementioned provision to provide a crystal clear mandate on succession by prohibiting certain local officials, who are disqualified by law to service during the prohibitive term, to fill permanent vacancies in elected positions covered by the prohibition.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MANDATORY PERIOD TO RELOCATE SQUATTERS, GRANTING DISTURBANCE FEE AND TAX EXEMPTION TO OWNER OF ILLEGALLY OCCUPIED RESIDENTIAL LAND, AND PENALIZING VIOLATION THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Landowners Protection Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Landowners Protection Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to provide a mandatory period in the relocation of squatters and to grant tax exemption to illegally occupied residential lands. It also seeks to compensate the landowners in case of failure of the local government unit (LGU) concerned to act on the request for assistance to evict illegal occupants within the prescribed period. The measure aims to provide equal protection to the squatters and to the landowners. It is intended to minimize, if not totally eliminate, squatting because LGUs will then be compelled to monitor vacant lands to prevent trespassers from constructing illegal structures therein.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C077
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09346) enacted on 2006-06-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7659 ENTITLED 'AN ACT TO IMPOSE THE DEATH PENALTY ON CERTAIN HEINOUS CRIMES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, OTHER SPECIAL PENAL LAWS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to abolish the imposition of death penalty in the country. Scientific evidence show that death penalty has not been instrumental in deterring crime. In fact, in the Philippines, the number of death row inmates continue to grow despite the execution of several death convicts already. The bill further advocates the reduction of the death penalty already imposed to reclusion perpetua.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE WAIVER OF THE RETIREMENT AGE REQUIREMENT OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE, WHO HAS RENDERED AT LEAST TWENTY (20)YEARS OF SERVICE, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1146, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM ACT OF 1977
rows.abstract: To enable to government to get rid of employees who no longer have the drive to perform efficiently as they are merely waiting for the right age to retire and to maintain fresh legs and minds in the service, this bill proposes to allow government employees to retire after serving the government for a period of twenty (20) years. This will open windows of opportunities for retirees to venture into other fields using the amounts received from their retirement benefits while still in their productive years.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FAIR AND EQUITABLE TERMS FOR THE RELEASE OF MEDICAL PRACTITIONERS' PROFESSIONAL FEE WITHHELD BY HOSPITALS OR MEDICAL CLINICS FOR FAILURE OF THE PATIENT TO PAY HOSPITAL BILLS AND PENALIZING VIOLATIONS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Medical Practitioners Protection Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Medical Practitioners Protection Act of 2004\". It is the practice in many hospitals to withhold the payment of professional fees of medical practitioners pending full settlement of patient's hospital bills. This bill seeks to extend protection to medical practitioners by instituting a mechanism that will ensure fair and equitable terms for the release of professional fees of medical practitioners withheld by hospitals or medical clinics because of the failure of a patient to pay his hospital bills.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-30, transmitted to on 2006-09-07 and received by the Senate on 2006-09-07

second_reading.remarks: The Body adopted the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks on the measure.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING PUBLIC OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES FROM SMOKING WITHIN THE WORK PREMISES DURING OFFICE HOURS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Public Officers and Employees Smoking Ban Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Public Officers and Employees Smoking Ban Act of 2004\". Civil Service Commission Memorandum Circular (MC) NO. 30, Series of 1991, bans public servants from smoking. Under the MC, the first violation would lead to a reprimand; a second violation, suspension; and a third violation, dismissal. However, this MC has been ignored. To put more teeth to this policy, this bill seeks to ban public officers and employees from smoking within the work premises during office hours. It proposes to impose a penalty of prision correccional or temporary disqualification from holding public office or both to any person found guilty of violating the provisions of the act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE CONCURRENCE OF THE LOCAL SCHOOL BOARD ON THE ASSIGNMENT OF DIVISION SUPERINTENDENTS, DISTRICT SUPERVISORS, SCHOOL PRINCIPALS AND OTHER SCHOOL OFFICIALS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 99, PARAGRAPH (d) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The ambiguous wordings of Section 99 of the Local Government Code has led to various interpretations on the subject provision and which in turn, has resulted in some cases of discord between local officials and the appointee of the Department of Education. To make the provisions crystal clear, this bill seeks to requires the concurrence of the local school board on the assignment of division superintendents, district supervisors, school principals and other school officials to a particular local government unit.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CERTAIN PERSON WHO MAY REGISTER AS A VOTER TO PRESENT ANY PROOF OF LEGAL RESIDENCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8189, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE VOTERS REGISTRATION ACT OF 1996, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: There are numerous cases where the number of election registrants in a particular residential unit far exceeds the ideal or reasonable number of residents for each of them to live comfortably in such dwelling. This bill seeks to require a person, residing in the property of another, to present some proof of legal residence upon registration as a voter. It also requires the Punong Barangay to attest to the certification issued by the landlord and to maintain a record of the actual number of residentes in a particular property or dwelling unit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT EMPOWERING THE LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS TO SCREEN AND RECOMMEND THE APPLICANTS TO TEACHING POSITIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to strengthen the ranking system in the appointment of school teachers by empowering the Local School Boards to screen and recommend applicants to any teaching position in their area of jurisdiction. The bill further requires the applicants to possess the necessary qualifications and standards set by the Department of Education.

rows.author: C077
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO APPLY THE SHARE OF THE PROCEEDS DERIVED FROM THE DEVELOPMENT AND UTILIZATION OF HYDROTHERMAL, GEOTHERMAL AND OTHER SOURCES OF ENERGY FOR ELECTRIFICATION OF OTHER AREAS WITHIN THE PROVINCE WHERE THE SOURCE OF ENERGY IS LOCATED, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 294 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.title_short: Authorizing Local Government Units to Apply the Share of the Proceeds Dervied from Hydrothermal, Geothermanl and other Sources of Energy
rows.abstract: More than two (2) decades after the electrification program was launced to implement the total electrification of the entire country, several areas in the countryside still do not have any supply of electricity. The failure of the program to provide electricity to the whole countryside can be traced to lack of funds. This bill seeks to authorize local government unit to apply the share of the proceeds derived from the development and utilization of hydrothermal, geothermal and other sources of energy for the electrification of other areas within the province where the source of energy is located.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-04-05, transmitted to on 2006-04-25 and received by the Senate on 2006-04-25

second_reading.remarks: Approved and reconsidered on Second Reading on Nov. 29, 2005. Again, approved and reconsidered on Nov. 30, 2005.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA FOR THE POOR
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for the Poor
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for the Poor\". It is the policy of the State to uplift the standard of living and quality of life of the poor and provide them with sustained opportunities for growth and development. This bill clearly defines the basic irreducible rights of the poor, to wit: a. the right to employment; b. the right to food; c. the right to free quality education; d. the right to shelter; and e. the right to free health services and medicine.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETENTION OF LIVE OR DEAD PATIENTS IN HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL CLINICS ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES
rows.title_short: Prohibiting the Detention of Live or Dead Patients in Hospitals and Medical Clinics for Nonpayment of Hospital Bills or Medical Expenses
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to stop the undesirable practice of hospitals and medical clinics of holding the release of fully recovered and/or dead patients because of non-payment, either partially or fully, of hospital bills. This practice has resulted in prolonged and, hence, more expensive stay of financially distressed patients in the hospitals. The bill allows underprivileged patients to leave the hospital upon the execution of a duly secured promissory note and imposes a penal sanction for any violation of the proposed act.

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks and adopted the amendments as embodied in the Committee Report.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND RESETTLEMENT, ABOLISHING THE EXISTING HOUSING AGENCIES, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004\". The bill focuses on the housing needs of the poor and the homeless. It proposes the creation of the Department of Housing and Resettlement, which shall serve as the primary agency that will prepare, integrate, coordinate and supervise plans, programs, projects and activities of the government relative to urban planning, development and renewal.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF REAL ESTATE SERVICE IN THE PHILIPPINES, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE A PROFESSIONAL REGULATORY BOARD OF REAL ESTATE SERVICE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines
rows.abstract: \"Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines\". The real estate industry plays a vital role in the economic development of the country. A real estate transaction has a multiplier effect on the country's economy. The bill elevates the real estate service practice. i.e., real estate brokerage, appraisal and consultancy, to the category of a profession, thereby placing realty service practitioners under the jurisdiction of the Professional Regulatory Commission. It also provides for the integration of all realty service practitioners under one national organization.

rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09484) enacted on 2007-06-02
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF DENTISTRY, DENTAL HYGIENE AND DENTAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4419, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF DENTISTRY IN THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES', AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 768, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF DENTAL HYGIENISTS IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES', APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: The Philippine Dental Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Philippine Dental Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to upgrade the total practice of the dentistry profession to keep pace with developments in the field and in allied disciplines, particularly the current focus on public health and safety which are also areas of concerns of the dentistry profession. The current practice of the dentistry profession is regulated by a 1965 legislation which the dentistry community deems not to have fully addressed the varied aspects of the practice of the profession.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PRE-SCHOOL LEARNING CENTER IN EACH OF THE FORTY-SIX (46) BARANGAYS IN THE FIRST DISTRICT OF CEBU CITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AND PROVIDING FOR FREE COLLEGE EDUCATION IN INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Free Information and Communications Technology College Education Act of 2001
rows.abstract: \"Free Information and Communications Technology College Education Act of 2001\". The measure seeks to provide free college education in information and communications technology (ICT), a two-year college degree course, to all high school graduates of public schools. These beneficiaries would have the right to choose the public or state college or university within the city, province or region where he may enroll to enjoy the free college education benefit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1869, EXPRESSLY EXCLUDING JAI-ALAI GAMES FROM THE FRANCHISED ACTIVITIES OF THE PHILIPPINE AMUSEMENT AND GAMING CORPORATION
rows.abstract: The bill expressly excludes jai-alai games from the franchised activities of the PAGCOR.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT STANDARDIZING AND UPGRADING THE BENEFITS FOR MILITARY VETERANS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS'
rows.abstract: It is disheartening to note that our war veterans receive a meager pension. With the continuing increase in the cost of living, most of them could hardly afford a decent and humane standard of living. This bill seeks to increase the present benefits of our Filipino World War veterans by increasing their monthly pension and at the same time provide them with medical assistance. It is hoped that the proposed benefits would help improve the quality of their lives.
rows.status: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2006-06-06

committee_action.action: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2006-06-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES TO ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS, INCLUDING BARANGAY TANODS AND MEMBERS OF THE LUPONG TAGAPAMAYAPA, AND BARANGAY EMPLOYEES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Barangay Incentives Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Barangay Incentives Act of 2004\". To give due recognition to the important job being performed by grassroots workers, this bill proposes to provide incentives to barangay officials, including barangay tanods and members of the lupong tagapamayapa and barangay empployees. Among the benefits being proposed in the bill are: a. exemption from income tax on salaries, wages, compensation, remuneration and other emoluments; b. exemption from capital gains and transfer taxes; c. GSIS benefit coverage; d. health benefits; and e. free legal representation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE VENUE OF THE CRIMINAL AND CIVIL ACTION IN LIBEL CASES AGAINST COMMUNITY JOURNALISTS, PUBLICATIONS OR BROADCAST STATIONS
rows.title_short: Providing for the Venue of the Criminal and Civil Action in Libel Cases AGainst Community Journalists, Publications or Broadcast Stations
rows.abstract: Under the present rule on venue, the complainant, if he is a public officer, can file the complaint in Manila if his office is in Manila or in the office outside Manila if his office is located there. This rule on venue has placed community journalists and local broadcasters in a situation where they have to answer complaints filed, rightly or wrongly, in distant places, diliberately filed far away from their place of work.  The bill seeks to provide a specific venue of action in libel cases against a community journalist, community publication or community broadcast station.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31

second_reading.remarks: On April 5, 2006, the Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks on the measure.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE SALARY GRADE OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS FROM SALARY GRADE 10 TO 20 AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Public school teachers are among the most underpaid workers in our society. Considering that teachers are the prime movers in the education system, the government should give priority to their interest and welfare. This measure seeks to upgrade the salary level of public school teachers in the elementary and secondary schools from Grade 10 to Grade 20.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PROHIBITED ACTS OF DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WOMEN ON ACCOUNT OF SEX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 135 AND 137 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to \"ensure the fundamental equality before the law of women and men\". Consistent with this mandate, the bill seeks to prohibit absolutely any act of employer or person, acting on behalf of the employer, from discriminating, directly or indirectly, against female employees or workers - or giving preference to male workers - in all matters pertaining to employment or employment opportunities and employment benefits. The prohibited acts shall include announcements, publications or advertisements of any kind or any form that would deny women equal employment opportunities.

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CIVIL SERVICE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Philippine Civil Service Code of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Civil Service Code of 2004\".   This bill seeks to update the existing laws, decrees, letters on instructions, executive orders and make them consistent with the needs of the present system of civil governance. It aims to address the deeply-rooted problems confronting the public service such as graft and corruption, bureaucratic red tape, violations of the rights of employees, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL HEALTH CODE OF 2004
rows.title_short: National Health Code of the Philippines of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Health Code of the Philippines of 2004\". The measure seeks to unify the health care delivery system of the country by emphasizing the meaningful partnership of each health component - the government units, the private sector, the nongovernment units and the community, which should perform to make health care available, accessible, acceptable and affordable. The Code will serve as an important directional reference and policy basis for planners, public and private administrators, program implementers, researchers and the general public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH THE DIMANPUDSO NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL IN BARANGAY DIMANPUDSO, MUNICIPALITY OF MARIA AURORA, PROVINCE OF AURORA, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO ARE ASSIGNED OUTSIDE OF THEIR TOWNS AND PROVINCES APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Public School Teachers' Incentives' Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Public School Teachers' Incentives' Act of 2004\". The Constitution provides for the State to \"assign the highest budgetary priority to education and ensure that teaching will attract and retain its rightful share of the best available talents through adequate remuneration and other means of job satisfaction and fulfillment\". Despite the above, the welfare of the teachers remain neglected. This measure proposes additional incentive to public school teachers who are assigned to towns other than their own town but within the same province. Those who are assigned to towns of other provinces shall be entitled to more incentives under the proposed bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA FOR THE INFORMAL SECTOR, INSTITUTIONALIZING MECHANISM FOR IMPLEMENTATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for the Informal Sector
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for the Informal Sector\". \"Informal sector\" refers to a specific sector in the economy where most of the participants are categorized as \"unregistered, undocumented, untaxed, uninsured, disorganized and doing irregular economic activities\". The informal sector comprises almost half of the country's total workforce. The proposed Code seeks to introduce an integrated, holistic and comprehensive policy instrument which shall serve as the springboard for the informal sector to join the mainstream of the Philippine economy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-11-08

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF THE NATIONAL HERITAGE, THE CREATION OF A NATIONAL HERITAGE COMMISSION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Heritage Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Heritage Act of 2004\". The Philippines is blessed with rich resources and heritage. However, the government's efforts to forestall the deterioration of our heritage has proven inadequate. This bill seeks to protect, preserve, conserve and promote the nation's cultural heritage, its properties and its histories. It also proposes the creation of the National Heritage Commission, which shall be tasked to promulgate rules and regulations pertaining to the conservation of our heritage, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF THE WORD 'MUSLIM' OR 'ISLAMIC' IN PRINT, RADIO, TELEVISION AND OTHER FORMS OF BROADCAST MEDIA TO REFER TO OR DESCRIBE ANY PERSON CONVICTED OF ANY CRIME, OR SUSPECTED OF COMMITTING ANY UNLAWFUL ACT, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The use of the words \"Muslim\" and \"Islamic\" in association with suspected or criminal and unalawful acts are offensively biased against Muslims. This practice is highly prejudicial and extremely injurious to the Islamic religious culture and to Muslim individuals. This measure prohibits the use of the word \"Muslim\" or \"Islamic\" in print, television and other forms of broadcast media to refer to or to describe any person convicted of a crime or suspected of committing any unlawful act. The outlawing of this biased practice would definitely help lessen enmity between Muslims and non-Muslims.

committee_action.remarks: Joint with Committee on Muslim Affairs

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A SCHOOL MODERNIZATION AND INNOVATION PROGRAM FOR PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: School Modernization and Innovation Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"School Modernization and Innovation Act of 2004\".   This bill aims to institutionalize a comprehensive modernization program for public schools and to provide a mechanism for the private sector and for local government units to participate in the program. The bill also seeks to establish the School Modernization and Innovation Trust Fund which will augment regular appropriations under the General Appropriations Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE LEGITIMATION OF CHILDREN BORN TO PARENTS BELOW MARRYING AGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Today, the incidents of children born out of wedlock to parents who are disqualified under the law to marry each other because of the issue of minority are still very common. To uphold the rights and dignity of these children, this bill provides for the legitimation of children born to parents below marrying age.

rows.author: E011
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROGRAM FOR THE ACQUISITION OF SCHOOL SITES AND THE CONSTRUCTION, MAINTENANCE, REHABILITATION, AND REPAIR OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS IN THE PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS NATIONWIDE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: School Building Program Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"School Building Program Act of 2004\".  This bill seeks to create a comprehensive program which will address the problem of classroom shortage. It carries a provision for a build-operate, build-lease-transfer, build-transfer, rehabilitate-operate-transfer and other contractual arragements that will allow the use of both government and private funds to finance the construction of school buildings. It is hoped that with the passage of the bill, class sizes will be reduced to a manageable level and thus result in the improvement in the quality of education.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING REFORMS IN LAND ADMINISTRATION, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LAND ADMINISTRATION AUTHORITY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Land Administration Reform Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Land Administration Reform Act of 2004\". In line with the government's program to institute reforms in the present land administration system, this measure seeks to consolidate and streamline land administration powers and functions within a single government agency to be known as the Land Administration Authority. Under the present system, land administration is dispersed across the Department of Justice; Land Registration Authority and Register of Deeds; the Department of Environment and Natural Resources; Lands Management Bureau; Land Management Services in the regional, provincial and community offices; National Mapping and Resource Information and the CARP Secretariat and its field offices.

rows.abstract: \"Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA)\". rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUVENILE JUSTICE, CREATING THE OFFICE OF JUVENILE JUSTICE AND DELINQUENCY PREVENTION UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Youth offenders should be treated differently from the way adult offenders are handled. This measure intends to provide a just and more humane system of treating juvenile offenders in society through a comprehensive and integrated approach toward rehabilitating the delinquency. In consonance with the provisions of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and the UN Standard Minimum Rules for the Administration of Juvenile Systems, the bill emphasizes on the need of rehabilitating and reintegrating the juvenile offender into the mainstream of society.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE YEARLY ALLOCATION FOR SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNOLOGICAL ACTIVITIES (STA)
rows.title_short: Science and Technology Funding Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Science and Technology Funding Act of 2004\". This bill seeks to allocate an amount equivalent to the prescribed UNESCO norm of at least one percent (1%) of the gross national product as the annual budget for scientific and technological activities (STA). It also proposes the allocation for the STA to gradually increase until it reaches the prescribed norm on the 5th year which shall include both government and private sector activities.
